title: Identification of the stratum root multisets
statement:
In the situation of [prop-galois-weight-strata], for each integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$ let $R_i$ be its specified weight-$i$ submultiset in $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ and define
$$
Q_i(T)=\prod_{\alpha\in R_i}(1-\alpha T)\in\overline{\mathbf Q}[T],
$$
with each occurrence of $\alpha$ contributing one factor. Then the reciprocal-root multiset of $Q_i$, equivalently the root multiset of $Q_i^\#(U)=U^{\deg Q_i}Q_i(U^{-1})$, is exactly the submultiset of the roots of $A^\#$ satisfying the weight-$i$ $q$-Weil condition when $i$ is odd, and exactly the submultiset of the roots of $B^\#$ satisfying that condition when $i$ is even. The multiset is therefore determined by the weight condition alone and does not depend on the ordering of the roots. Reciprocal roots are counted with the multiplicity of their inverses as ordinary roots, as in [lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization]; $Q_i^\#$ is the coefficient-reversal polynomial of [lem-weil-reciprocal-polynomial].

proof.text: Fix $i$ in the stated range and enumerate the finite multiset $R_i$ as $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n$, keeping repetitions. By its definition in [prop-galois-weight-strata], every entry satisfies the $q$-Weil condition of [def-weil-numbers], which is a condition on $\overline{\mathbf Q}^{\times}$; hence every $\alpha_j$ is nonzero. Expanding the defining product gives $Q_i(0)=1$, no terms above degree $n$, and coefficient $(-1)^n\prod_{j=1}^n\alpha_j\ne0$ in degree $n$. Thus $\deg Q_i=n$. By coefficient reversal, $Q_i^\#(0)$ is that same nonzero coefficient, so zero is not a root of $Q_i^\#$. These assertions include $n=0$: $Q_i=Q_i^\#=1$.

source.place: ## Proof: reciprocal-root identification, expanded using the definition of Q_i in the neighboring prop-galois-weight-strata-integrality statement

proof.text: Apply clause 3 of [lem-weil-reciprocal-root-factorization] with $K=L=\overline{\mathbf Q}$, coefficient homomorphism the identity, and $P=Q_i$. Its hypotheses hold: this is an algebraically closed field, $Q_i(0)=1$, and the displayed product has exactly $n=\deg Q_i$ nonzero parameters by step 1. For every $\alpha\ne0$, the number of occurrences of $\alpha$ in that product, namely its multiplicity in $R_i$, equals both the multiplicity of $\alpha^{-1}$ as a root of $Q_i$ and the multiplicity of $\alpha$ as a root of $Q_i^\#$. The first is its reciprocal-root multiplicity by the same lemma. Zero occurs in none of these multisets by step 1. Equality of all occurrence counts gives equality of the reciprocal-root multiset, the root multiset of $Q_i^\#$, and $R_i$.

source.place: ## Proof: reciprocal-root identification, expanded using the definition of Q_i in the neighboring prop-galois-weight-strata-integrality statement

proof.text: By the displayed definition of $R_i$ in [prop-galois-weight-strata], it is the weight-$i$ submultiset of roots of $A^\#$ for odd $i$ and of $B^\#$ for even $i$. Substituting this definition in step 2 gives both parity cases of the claim. Explicitly, the count of any $\alpha$ in $R_i$ is its count in the relevant polynomial's root multiset if it satisfies the weight condition, and zero otherwise. This formula depends on the polynomial and predicate, not on an enumeration. Also, permuting an enumeration merely permutes the factors of the commutative product defining $Q_i$. Hence the resulting multiset is independent of all root orderings. No appeal to Galois descent or integrality of $Q_i$ is needed.
